_README: FROZEN Lighthouse baseline — the score FLOOR enforced by
Semantics: floors.<slug>.<category> = the MINIMUM score (0-100) that route may
report for that category. The reported score is the MEDIAN of LH_REPEATS passes.
Measured < floor => CI FAILS. A route present in
screenshotMatrix.ts::TARGET_PAGES but absent from `floors` FAILS too — an
unbaselined route is a hole, not a pass.
This is a RATCHET: the floor may only ever RISE. It is today's measured score
with no margin subtracted. Lowering a floor is a deliberate, written trade-off,
never a way to make CI green — the same rule as a11y-baseline.json.
`accessibility` is NOT a category here and never will be. axe-core owns that
question (a11y-baseline.json, per-page per-rule node ceilings, adjudicated in
is evidence for the A-08 screen-reader audit.

provenance.measured_by: GitHub Actions — E2E workflow, job 'Lighthouse — score ratchet vs. the seeded stack (RC P11-8)'
provenance.conditions: seeded Compose stack (SEED_E2E_GOLDEN + SEED_ESP_TA + SEED_RATIONALE), Admin session, 1440x900 desktop form factor, simulated throttling at Lighthouse's own desktop preset (rttMs 40, throughputKbps 10240, cpuSlowdownMultiplier 1), maxWaitForLoad 20000 ms, median of 3 passes per route after a discarded warm-up
provenance.measured_pre_merge: Measured on the P11-8 branch, not on main: the whole point of the run was to record the tree WITH the gate in it. The next main run must reproduce these numbers exactly — if it does not, this file is wrong, not the run.
provenance.stability: Worst repeat spread was 0 points in every category on all 23 routes. That is why the floor is the measured score with NO margin subtracted: there is no noise here to leave room for. If a future run starts flapping, the answer is more repeats or a warm-up change — never a lower floor.
provenance.sensitivity_boundary: performance sits at 100 on 22 of 23 routes. That is a real measurement, not a rounding artefact, and it is also this gate's weakest axis: against a localhost stack on the desktop preset the score is saturated, so only a substantial regression will move it. A floor of 100 means 'may not get worse at all' — the strictest ratchet available — but it is not evidence that the app is fast on a real user's machine. The per-route FCP/LCP/TBT/CLS/SI in lighthouse-report/lighthouse-results.json do differentiate the routes and are reported, never gated.

policy.accessibility: NOT REQUESTED — axe-core is the shipped a11y authority (frontend/e2e/a11y-baseline.json). Two competing a11y numbers would be two authorities. No Lighthouse output is A-08 evidence.
policy.performance_vs_loadgen: Lighthouse measures the BROWSER (paint, interactivity, layout stability of a route). scripts/loadgen.py measures the SERVER (per-endpoint HTTP p95, control-normalised, nightly ratio gate). docs/performance/README.md section 8 names frontend rendering as out of the load driver's scope; this file covers exactly that declared gap. Neither number may be cited for the other's question.
policy.margin: none — the floor is the measured median, not the median minus a cushion. Noise is answered by repeats + median, never by widening the band.
